step.cmd: In Curam, review the letter in question as follows:

ul.li: From the Application Case, select Contacts from the navigation bar.
Select Communications from the menu on the left-hand side of the screen.
Select > beside the letter in question.
Select the 3 dots ( … ) on the right side of the screen, beside Edit . From the drop-down menu, select Preview .
Letters not sent from Curam are reviewed from ACS.

step.cmd: Determine the type of undeliverable mail that was returned:

ul.li: If the undeliverable mail is a D-80 -00-00 letter, go to step 3.

If the undeliverable mail is a D-91-00-00 warning letter that includes an unclassified violation, (in Curam on the Violation evidence, the Type field shows Violation - warning letter issued ), go to step 5.
If the undeliverable mail is a notice of decision that set up an OP or a penalty, go to step 8.
If the undeliverable mail is a D-91-00-00 letter that does not include an unclassified violation (In Curam, on the Violation evidence, the Type field shows Warning Letter ), go to step 8.
If the undeliverable mail is a notice of decision unrelated to a Notice of Debt, go to step 9.
If the undeliverable mail is any other ACS letter, go to step 10.
If the undeliverable mail is a I-10-00-00 letter containing the client’s access code, go to step 11.
If the undeliverable mail is a benefit statement with an access code, go to step 11.
If the undeliverable mail is none of the above, go to step 10.

step.cmd: Review and recreate the undeliverable D-80-00-00 letter as follows:

ul.li: From the Person Case, select the Contacts tab from the navigation bar.
Select Communications from the left side menu.
Locate the undelivered D-80-00-00 letter from the list of correspondence and select the 3 dots ( … ) on the right side to preview the letter.

step.cmd: In ACS, create and send the N-70-00-00 letter with the same information as communicated in the original D-80-00-00 letter. Go to step 13.
Determine if there is an OP related to the D-91-00-00 warning letter that includes an unclassified violation:

ul.li: If no, go to step 6.
If yes, go to step 8.

step.cmd: In Curam, update the Violation evidence with a new Notification Week as follows:

ul.li: From the Application Case, select Evidence from the navigation bar.
Locate the Violation evidence from the Qualification/Calculation Related row on the Evidence Dashboard .
Select the Violation to open the evidence and select Edit from the right hand-side.
On the Notification Week field, enter today’s date.
Select Save .

step.cmd: In ACS, create and send a new D-91-00-00 decision letter with the same information as the original decision. Go to step 13.
Determine if the Notice of Debt that is related to the undeliverable notice of decision was returned as undeliverable:

ul.li: If the Notice of Debt was not returned as undeliverable, go to step 9.
If the Notice of Debt was returned as undeliverable, go to step 13.

step.cmd: From the appropriate electronic system (i.e. ACS, FTS, Imaging) print a copy of the undeliverable mail.
Address an envelope with the client’s new address, enclose the undeliverable mail and send it to the client. Go to step 13.
Determine if the access code has been reissued:

ul.li: If no, go to step 12.
If yes, go to step 15.

step.cmd: In Curam re-issue the access code as follows:

ul.li: From the Person Case, select Home from the navigation bar.
From the Home screen, under Access Code , the first 2 digits of the client’s access code are displayed, along with the date the original code was issued.
Select the 3 dots ( … ) on the right side and select Re-Issue from the drop-down menu.
Select Save .

step.cmd: In NWS, add details to the draft SROC created during fact-finding or create a new SROC as follows:

ul.li: Main Issue: Select Undeliverable Mail .
Comments: Type “Curam claim. Undeliverable mail – new address confirmed.”

Details: Type one of the following options:
“[Type of undeliverable mail] originally sent [date] received as undeliverable on [date] — resent to the client’s new address.” Also document if the original letter was a D-80-00-00 letter sent from Curam and if a N-70-00-00 or F-00-00-00 letter has been sent instead.
“Notice of decision not resent to the client’s new address as the Notice of Debt was also undeliverable.”
“Access code reissued.” Also document if the original letter was a I-10-00-00 letter sent from Curam and if a F-00-00-00 letter has been sent instead.
Document the fact-finding details according to the National Fact-Finding and Documentation Policy . National Fact-Finding and Documentation Policy
Select Save .

step.cmd: In Curam, document the actions taken as follows:

ul.li: Return to the Correspondence Failed – Undeliverable Mail task.

Select Add Comments and type the appropriate option:
“[Type of undeliverable mail] originally sent [date] received as undeliverable on [date] — resent to the client’s new address.” Also document if the original letter was a D-80-00-00 letter sent from Curam and if the N-70-00-00 or F-00-00-00 letter has been sent instead.
“Notice of decision not resent to the client’s new address as the Notice of Debt was also undeliverable.”
“Access code reissued.” Also document if the original letter was a I-10-00-00 letter sent from Curam and if a F-00-00-00 letter has been sent instead.
Select Save .

step.cmd: In Cúram, complete the task as follows:

ul.li: From the Correspondence Failed – Undeliverable Mail task, select the 3 dots ( … ) at the top right-hand corner of the screen.
From the drop-down menu, select Complete .
Select Yes .

step.cmd: In NWS, determine if an AI WI exists for the Curam correspondence issue?

ul.li: If yes, complete the AI WI and go to step 17.
If no, go to step 17.

step.cmd: In NWS, determine if there are any other WIs on file for additional letters received as Undeliverable?

ul.li: If yes, action each impacted letter.
If no, no further action required.
